subject: Security notification: transient auth spike — SOC 2 evidence request and IR playbook coordination
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Lopez <sarah.lopez@finadvisory.com>, security-ops@finadvisory.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Security notification: transient auth spike — SOC 2 evidence request and IR playbook coordination

Hi Sarah / FinAdvisory security team,

Quick note to notify you that we observed a short-lived spike in authentication failures for a small subset of FinAdvisory tenant keys between 2026-12-14T08:40:00Z and 2026-12-14T08:56:00Z. We contained the activity within our edge layer and rotated the affected API keys at 08:58Z. No customer data was accessed; the spike appears to be credential stuffing against an older API key issued in 2024 (now revoked).

What we're sending now: a curated evidence bundle for your SOC 2 audit and for your internal review. Attached items in the next email include: a compressed log export (auth and token issuance), a redacted postmortem draft, a sampled S3 access list for the time range, and a CSV timeline of events.

Next steps we propose:
- Schedule a 30-min call today to walk through the artifacts and answer auditor questions (I have availability 11:30–12:30 PT).
- We will provide a limited SFTP drop and a Drive folder with signed checksums for the attached archives.
- If your SOC 2 auditor needs a different retention view or additional telemetry (e.g., full VPC flow samples), let us know and we can coordinate a discrete export.

We are treating this as an incident for evidence purposes and will share the finalized postmortem and retention notes after your review/redaction request.

Attachments (stubs to follow):
- forensic_log_export_20261214.tar.gz (auth logs, token issuance events, anonymized IPs)
- ir_postmortem_redacted_20261214.pdf (draft)
- s3_access_sample_20261214.csv (sampled access entries)
- timeline_events_20261214.csv (event-level timeline)

Thanks — Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Sarah Lopez <sarah.lopez@finadvisory.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Thomas Kaplan <thomas.kaplan@atlas-audit.com>, security-ops@finadvisory.com, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 09:35:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Security notification: transient auth spike — SOC 2 evidence request and IR playbook coordination

Rafael — thanks for the heads up and for putting together the artifacts. Thomas (our SOC 2 lead) is copied. Two quick asks from our side before we sync: 

1) Can you confirm whether any refresh tokens or long-lived tokens were rotated or used during the window? Our scope requires confirmation of token lifecycle actions.
2) Please include an inventory of affected keys (obfuscated if needed) and the exact revocation timestamp. Thomas will need the revocation hash for cross-checking.

We can take a 30-minute call at 12:00 PT. Prefer a short walk-through and then separate the artifacts for the auditor.

Thanks — Sarah
Sarah Lopez
Security Lead, FinAdvisory
sarah.lopez@finadvisory.com

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Lopez <sarah.lopez@finadvisory.com>, Thomas Kaplan <thomas.kaplan@atlas-audit.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Security notification: transient auth spike — SOC 2 evidence request and IR playbook coordination

Thanks Sarah — answers inline below and I uploaded the initial bundle to the Drive and SFTP locations listed at the bottom. I also added Thomas to make the auditor hand-off explicit.

1) Token lifecycle: We observed only short-lived access token failures. No refresh tokens were exchanged during the window. There were no refresh-token-based session escalations tied to the affected key IDs. We rotated the older API key (key id suffix abcd) at 2026-12-14T08:58:27Z (revocation propagated to edge in ~20s). Revocation record: revocation_hash: sha256:3f7a2e... (full hash in the Drive manifest).

2) Affected keys: Inventory attached as a redacted list (first 6/8 hex characters only). See file inventory_affected_keys_20261214.csv in the Drive.

What I uploaded to the evidence locations:
- Drive: https://drive.redwood.example.com/finadvisory/2026-12-14-ir-evidence (read-only link, auditor view)
- SFTP: sftp://evidence.redwood.example.com/finadvisory/20261214/ (one-time creds shared out-of-band)
- Files in bundle: forensic_log_export_20261214.tar.gz, ir_postmortem_redacted_20261214.pdf, s3_access_sample_20261214.csv, timeline_events_20261214.csv, inventory_affected_keys_20261214.csv

Data handling note: logs are pseudonymized (IP addresses replaced with hashed prefixes) per our evidence-sharing policy; full raw logs can be produced under a mutual NDA amendment if your legal/audit team requires them.

I'll join the 12:00 PT call. Marissa, Ben — I've included the primary asks below so we can cover them on the call.

-- Rafael

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Security notification: transient auth spike — SOC 2 evidence request and IR playbook coordination

Thanks Rafael / Sarah — for the call, our agenda will be:

1) Confirm scope of artifacts Thomas needs for SOC 2 (we'll confirm whether sampled telemetry is sufficient).
2) Walk through the redacted postmortem and the revocation timeline.
3) Clarify retention and redaction requirements (what FinAdvisory needs for auditor vs what we publish in a customer-facing postmortem).
4) Actions and ownerships: (a) Ben: finalize checksum and SFTP drop; (b) Rafael: prepare brief notes on token lifecycle; (c) Marissa: prepare retention exception request if full raw logs are requested.

Ben — can you upload the signed checksums and set the SFTP folder to expire after 7 days?

Sarah / Thomas — files are in place. SFTP creds were shared via the separate secure channel you requested; Drive link above is read-only for auditor accounts. Checksums: sha256 sums included in checksums_20261214.txt. SFTP folder will expire on 2026-12-21T23:59:00Z.

I also attached the current redacted postmortem (ir_postmortem_redacted_20261214.pdf) in this thread for your review; it contains timeline, root cause hypothesis, mitigation steps, and a short note on monitoring improvements we will deploy next week.
